title: Noetherian approximation preserving flatness and geometrically integral fibres
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a finitely presented flat homomorphism of commutative rings whose fibre rings $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are geometrically integral over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] [def-weil-residue-field] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Then there exist a cocartesian diagram of commutative rings $R_0\to S_0$, $R_0\to R$, $S_0\to S$ with $R_0$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, $R_0\to S_0$ of finite type and flat, and every fibre ring $S_0\otimes_{R_0}\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)$, $\mathfrak p_0$ a prime of $R_0$, geometrically integral over $\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)$; the given rings are recovered by $S\cong S_0\otimes_{R_0}R$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-subring-model-system] to the given flat finitely presented map $R\to S$. Obtain $i,B_i,j_f$ and $B_j=B_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j$. On the tail $j\geq j_f$, the base rings have colimit $R$, every $R_j$ is a finite-type integer subalgebra, every $R_j\to B_j$ is finitely presented and flat, and the compatible isomorphisms $B_j\otimes_{R_j}R\cong S$ identify the original algebra map with the base change. In particular the chosen model is part of one fixed compatible family.

source.place: Tag 05FE, lemma-Noetherian-approximation-flat, proof via lemma-Noetherian-approximation-flat-module: the flat algebra-model construction, expanded to its cofinal subalgebra system and compatible cocartesian squares.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-geometrically-integral-fibres-limit-descent] to the small directed tail $j\geq j_f$ supplied by [lem-trf-flat-subring-model-system], taking $a=j_f$, $A_j=R_j$, $A=R$ and $C_a=B_{j_f}$. Write $C=C_a\otimes_{R_{j_f}}R$. The tower statement identifies $C_a\otimes_{R_{j_f}}R_j$ with $B_j$ and $C_a\otimes_{R_{j_f}}R$ with $S$ as an $R$-algebra. For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, tensoring the latter isomorphism with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ gives the fibre isomorphism $C\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, sending $c\otimes t$ to $\theta_{j_f}(c)\otimes t$, with inverse induced by $\theta_{j_f}^{-1}$. For every field extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ the same formulas, tensored with $K$, give inverse $K$-algebra isomorphisms, so nonemptiness, reducedness and irreducibility hold on both sides simultaneously. Thus the original geometric fibre hypothesis applies exactly. Take $j_0$ to be the threshold supplied by descent. Its conclusion applies to $C_{j_0}=B_{j_f}\otimes_{R_{j_f}}R_{j_0}$. The tower gives an $R_{j_0}$-algebra isomorphism $C_{j_0}\cong B_{j_0}$; tensoring this isomorphism and its inverse with each $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and each extension of that field identifies their geometric fibres. Hence $R_{j_0}\to B_{j_0}$ has geometrically integral fibres at every prime, including primes outside the image of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. No surjectivity of a colimit projection is used.

proof.text: Set $R_0=R_{j_0}$ and $S_0=B_{j_0}$. The conclusions of [lem-trf-flat-subring-model-system] give finite type of $R_0$ over $\mathbf Z$, flatness of $R_0\to S_0$, and the compatible cocartesian square with $S_0\otimes_{R_0}R\cong S$. Its finite presentation expresses $S_0$ as a quotient of $R_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ by finitely many relations [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; the images of the variables generate it, giving the required finite type. Together with step 2 this verifies every condition of the claimed diagram.
